title: Management of Time and Energy
summary: Time and energy are limited resources used together. Time is equal for everyone (24 hours); energy is the capacity to do work and differs from person to person. Making the best use of them is time and energy management; taking a short cut saves both.

A time plan or schedule is an advance plan of what we are going to do in a given period. Steps: (1) list all the activities; (2) group them into flexible activities (shopping – can be shifted) and inflexible activities (school, classes – fixed time); (3) estimate the time required for each activity; (4) balancing – adjusting the time of activities so that the total fits the available time (reduce time on some activities; start with activities that take long). Points to keep in mind: a schedule easy to follow, practical and flexible, an alternative plan for emergencies, time for rest and leisure, dovetailing. Peak load periods are times of the day when many activities have to be done in a fixed time (morning); manage them by pre-preparation (iron uniforms and prepare food in the evening). Leisure period is the rest and hobby time that recharges the body and relieves stress. Family members' plans that clash are adjusted (bathing order).

Advantages of a time plan: finish all work efficiently without tiredness; find time for rest and hobbies; do more productive and better quality work in less time; avoid last-minute tension and confusion; time for unforeseen events such as visitors or illness. Ways to save time: follow the plan, do not waste time, use labour-saving equipment, and dovetail.

Dovetailing is doing two or three activities at the same time. Example: cooking dal and vegetables, washing dishes and washing clothes one after another takes 20 + 20 + 20 + 20 = 80 minutes; by dovetailing (start the washing machine, put the dal on to boil, cut vegetables while washing runs, wash dishes while cooking) the same work takes 5 + 2 + 5 + 10 + 20 + 5 + 8 = 55 minutes, saving 25 minutes.

Heavy activities need much energy (running, jogging, mopping, Diwali cleaning, cycling); moderate need an average amount (sweeping, ironing, cooking, preparing notes); light need very little (reading, watching TV, listening to music, telling a story). Fatigue can be physical or mental. Ways to save energy (work simplification): break a task into smaller activities (washing clothes: separate, soak, rub, rinse, dry); cut extra movements and combine activities (serve all glasses on a tray; clear the table in one or two trips); do activities in a better order (sweep before hanging clothes; dust before sweeping the floor is wrong); be skilled; use the correct posture (long-handled broom instead of bending, sit erect while studying); work at proper heights and keep things near the place of use (put things back); use labour-saving devices (mixer, toaster).

Give any four suggestions to smoothly carry out household activities at home.

Make a time plan; break big tasks into smaller activities; cut unnecessary movements by carrying things together on a tray; do activities in the right order; use the correct posture; keep things near the place of use and put them back; use labour-saving devices; share work among family members.

Explain the terms 'peak load' and 'dovetailing' with one example each.

Peak load: a period in the day when many activities must be done in a fixed time, e.g. the morning rush to get children ready for school. Dovetailing: doing two or more activities at the same time, e.g. putting dal on the stove and washing clothes in the machine while cutting vegetables.

Your brother gets tired while cleaning his room. Tell him four ways by which he gets tired.

Working in a wrong posture (bending for long); making unnecessary movements; doing activities in the wrong order (dusting before sweeping); working at an uncomfortable height; keeping things far away; not taking rest or breaking the task into parts.
October 2025
By dovetailing, the work of cooking dal, cooking vegetables, washing dishes and washing clothes (20 minutes each) was finished in 55 minutes. How much time was saved?
Without dovetailing: 20 + 20 + 20 + 20 = 80 minutes. With dovetailing: 55 minutes. Time saved = 80 – 55 = 25 minutes.
sa: Many household activities can be avoided to save energy. Identify any three such activities. Give one suggestion each to improve these.

(1) Going to the kitchen again and again to bring things – put all items on a tray and bring them in one trip. (2) Bending to sweep with a short broom – use a long-handled broom. (3) Searching for things – keep things at their places near where they are used. (4) Ironing or cooking at a wrong height – raise the working surface to a comfortable height.
Your sister complains of backache. Give her any six suggestions to save energy while doing household chores.

Sit or stand erect and do not bend for long; use a long-handled broom and mop; work at a comfortable height (ironing table, kitchen counter); keep things near the place of use; break the task into smaller activities with rests in between; use labour-saving devices like a mixer; dovetail activities and share work with family members.
Identify any three bad postures of your mother while doing household chores. Suggest one way in each case to improve them.

(1) Bending to sweep with a short broom – use a long-handled broom. (2) Sitting on the floor to iron or cook – work at a table or counter of comfortable height. (3) Stretching up to reach things stored too high – keep things within easy reach near the place of use.
Your family is always short of time. Tell your family members six benefits of making a time plan.

You finish work efficiently without feeling tired; get time for rest; get time for hobbies; do more productive work in less time; are saved from last-minute tension and confusion; get time for unforeseen events like guests or illness; the quality of work improves.
la: Explain the steps in making a time plan and how dovetailing helps to save time.

Steps: list all the activities; group them as flexible (shopping) and inflexible (school, classes); estimate the time for each; balance the time by reducing time on some activities so the total fits within 24 hours. A good plan is practical and flexible, has an alternative for emergencies and allows rest and leisure. Dovetailing means doing two or three activities together: cooking dal, cooking vegetables, washing dishes and washing clothes take 80 minutes separately but only 55 minutes when dovetailed (starting the washing machine, boiling dal, cutting vegetables meanwhile), saving 25 minutes.
Describe five ways of saving energy while doing household activities.

(1) Break the task into smaller activities (washing clothes: sort, soak, rub, rinse, dry). (2) Cut extra movements and combine activities (serve glasses on a tray). (3) Do activities in the proper order (sweep before dusting is wrong – dust first, then sweep). (4) Be skilled and use the correct posture (long-handled broom, sit erect). (5) Work at proper heights and keep things near the place of use. (6) Use labour-saving devices such as a mixer grinder.
